## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Lakhumāvimānavatthu* (Vv 19), rendered in English as "Lakhumā’s Mansion," is a verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral]. In this narrative, a deity explains how her meritorious actions in a previous human existence led to rebirth in a celestial mansion and the attainment of the fruit of a once-returner (*sakadāgāmī*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records thematic and textual associations with several other *vimāna* discourses (including Vv 15, Vv 22–25, Vv 37, and Vv 52), the *Revatīpetavatthu* (Pv 39), *Mittātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.7), Jātaka stories (Ja 489, Ja 541), and suttas from the Aṅguttara and Saṁyutta Nikāyas (AN 3.37, AN 3.38, SN 10.5) [SuttaCentral].
Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, with 201 passages matching across 35 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. In addition to extensive sharing with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §1.1–12.4), the text exhibits recurring formulaic verse material found in other *Vimānavatthu* narratives, most extensively *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33, segments §0.4–4.4), *Uposathāvimānavatthu* (Vv 24), *Uttarāvimānavatthu* (Vv 15), and *Soṇadinnāvimānavatthu* (Vv 23) [DharmaNexus]. Textual reuse is also detected in narrative verse segments shared with the *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541, segments §6.3–8.4) and the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
